html:
Spanish colonist, priest and Dominican friar who spent fifty years exposing the abuse of Indigenous peoples in the Americas and fighting for their rights.

He went to Hispaniola in 1502 and held an encomienda, a grant of Indigenous labourers. In 1514, after hearing the friars' sermons against these grants, he gave up his own and began to campaign at the Spanish court. He became a Dominican friar in 1523 and later bishop of Chiapas.

His campaigns helped bring about the New Laws of 1542. In 1550 and 1551 he argued at the Valladolid debate against the scholar Juan Ginés de Sepúlveda, who held that Indigenous people were natural slaves. His Short Account of the Destruction of the Indies (1552) was translated across Europe.

Early on he suggested bringing enslaved Africans to spare Indigenous workers. He later regretted it and condemned African slavery too, but the Atlantic slave trade was already growing.
sum: Spanish colonist, priest and Dominican friar who spent fifty years exposing the abuse of Indigenous peoples in the Americas and fighting for their rights.
